To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the properties of the TMPpyP cations in layered silicates are strongly influenced by the structure of the inorganic matrix and that this influence can be used for the design of hybrid materials with the desired photochemical properties of the TMPYpP dye.
the spectral properties of the TMPyp cation can be tuned by changing the nature of the layered silicate matrix and by modifying the interlayer space of the silicate.

layered silicate materials containing TMPyP cation can be obtained with the use of various methods and that they exhibit spectral properties of TMPyP cions that differ from those of TMPyP in solutions and colloidal suspensions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the preparation and characterization of the hybrid materials based on layered silicate with a porphyrin photosensitizer.
the development of new materials based on layered silicate and photochemically active TMPyP cation.
the preparation of new materials, which can be used in the field of photovoltaics and photocatalysis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the spectral changes of the porphyrin are caused by the flattening of the cationic pyrydinium substituents in the TMPyP molecule, which occurs in the presence of a silicate matrix.

the spectral changes in the TMPyP spectra are due to the structural changes in the dye molecules adsorbed onto the surface of layered silicates, which are induced by the interactions between the dye cations and the silicate surface.

the layered silicates can be considered as a versatile template for preparing the hybrid materials of variable spectral and photochemical properties of the porphyrin component, which is an important feature in the design of photochemically active materials.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the spectral properties of TMPyP cation in the hybrid materials are strongly dependent on the structural properties of the inorganic matrix and the method of preparation.
it is possible to prepare hybrid materials based on layered silicate and photochemically active TMPyP cation.
we were able to prepare and characterize layered materials with photochemically and spectroscopically active porphirin cations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the spectral properties of the TMPpyP molecules in the layered silicate films can be tailored by the preparation method and that the photochemical activity can be preserved.
the spectral properties of porphyrin dyes in layered silicate materials can be controlled and tailored for various purposes.
the spectral properties of TMPyP can be tailored to a great extent by changing the chemical composition and structure of the inorganic host.
